arguments.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer game sprite. Draw exactly ONE gull carrying clothes, isolated on actual transparent RGBA background. This is GJGULL2 frame 038.
Input 1: exact original sprite, sole authority for pose geometry, wing phase, yaw, eye visibility, carried cloth shape and overlap. Input 2: approved standing gull identity/style ONLY; do not copy its standing pose, large feet or ground shadow. Input 3: flat white ragged cloth MATERIAL/style ONLY; source input1 controls exact carrying orientation and size.
Specific original pose: Left-facing banking profile, one visible eye. Beak at left, tail at right. One wing reaches high up-right; opposite wing reaches down-left. Clothes trail diagonally down-right from the beak beneath the body. This is the reverse-facing view, not a right-facing head on a left-facing body.
Match the original's relative silhouette and occupied proportions closely, translating pixel anatomy into smooth clean cartoon shapes. The beak must physically pinch the cloth at the source attachment point; cloth hangs/trails below it as in input1, not tied to a foot or floating separately. The bundle is empty white clothing with pale cool-gray folds, crisp black outline and modest ragged edges. Preserve visible openings/folds and distinguish cloth from the feathered wings. No human skin, hands, arms or legs inside the clothing. Do not add a stick, hat, nest or props absent from input1.
Gull identity: white head and belly, light gray back and wings, charcoal-black feather tips, warm yellow-orange beak and small tucked webbed feet only where visible in the flying original; round dark eye(s) in the correct source positions. Crisp black cartoon outlines, restrained clean cel shading like input2. No extra wings or legs, no exaggerated new expression, no silhouette redesign. Keep the exact source facing and wing angles; do not make each phase identical.
Composition: complete sprite with about 5 percent clear transparent margin around every wingtip, tail, cloth edge and beak. No cropping. Keep the original's wide/tall aspect of the subject rather than stretching anatomy. Actual transparent background, no scenery, ground, shadows, glow, text, border or checkerboard.
CRITICAL CLOTH GEOMETRY: input3 is ONLY a white fabric color/shading sample. Do NOT turn the cloth into a long vertical hanging arrangement. Draw the carrying clothes in input1's exact footprint relative to bird, keeping the original diagonal trailing direction for profiles and the compact foreshortened bundle for fronts. Small original clothing must stay small. The source wing silhouette and beak-to-cloth relationship outrank both style inputs.
